findings.description: This subnet automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses to launched instances and is associated with a route table that has a default route to an internet gateway. Instances launched here can become directly internet-reachable if their security groups permit it.

This subnet automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses to launched instances and is associated with a route table that has a default route to an internet gateway. The portal server is launched in this subnet, increasing its direct internet exposure.
The EBS volume does not enable encryption. Data written to the attached portal disk may be stored unencrypted at rest unless encryption is imposed externally by an account-level default.

The user-data script embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. User data is accessible to privileged instance users and can be retrieved through the instance metadata service, exposing long-lived credentials to an attacker who compromises the host.

SSH port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0. Because the instance is in a public subnet and receives a public IP, this exposes remote administrative access to internet-wide scanning and password/key attack attempts.

The security group permits all protocols and ports to every IPv4 destination. This provides unrestricted egress for a compromised web server, facilitating data exfiltration and command-and-control communications.

The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs does not configure server-side encryption. Sensitive network metadata may be stored unencrypted at rest unless account-level default encryption is enforced externally.
The snapshot is created from an EBS volume that does not enable encryption, so the backup is also unencrypted at rest. This leaves copied disk data without EBS encryption protection.
